narrative:
Based on your profile, the model estimates that you have a 57 percent chance of failing your final year. That means the risk is real, but it is not a guarantee of failure; rather, it tells us that the factors visible in your situation point more strongly toward difficulty than toward success. Because of this, the school requires you to take remedial courses as a safety net.

The strongest factor pushing the prediction toward failing was your record of past course failures. You have one previous failure, while students who ultimately passed had, on average, none. Past failure is a meaningful signal because it often reflects gaps in knowledge or study habits that can carry forward, but it is also something that can be overcome with targeted help.

The second most important factor was your mother’s education level. Your mother completed only primary school, while most students who passed had mothers with higher education. This is not a judgment of your family. Statistically, students in this situation tend to have fewer academic resources or less direct help with schoolwork at home, which can make studying more challenging.

The third factor, family relationships, worked in your favor. You described your family relationships as good, and this pattern is common among students who pass. It suggests you have emotional support and a stable home environment, which reduces risk. However, this positive influence was not strong enough to outweigh the first two risk factors.

Use the remedial courses to close the gaps from your earlier failure and build stronger study routines. Lean on your family’s support and talk to teachers whenever something feels unclear. By doing so, you can turn this warning into a fresh start.
